newsitem.title: UK: Transco tenders to sell 5.38 TW/H gas on July 1.
newsitem.headline: Transco tenders to sell 5.38 TW/H gas on July 1.

text.p: UK gas pipeline operator Transco has issued a tender to sell 5.38 terawatt-hours (TWH) of natural gas on July 1, according to a copy of the tender document obtained by Reuters.
Of this total 0.184 TWH will be made available at Partington, in northwest England, and 5.197 TWH will be sold at the Rough storage facility off northeastern England.
The volume of 5.38 TWH is equivalent aproximately to 180 million therms.
The tender closes on June 20 and will be awarded on June 24, the document said, adding that the transfer date for the gas is July 1.

Transco originally said it would sell the gas under a variety of options in a phased disposal through the summer. Part of the sale would take place simply as a transfer of ownership of gas within existing storage facilities on July 1, August 1 and September 1.

The rest of the gas would have been sold on the over-the-counter gas market on a daily basis through July, August and September, at the National Balance Point, a notional node within the pipeline network which is increasingly becoming the focus of trade.

But these options were not available to Transco, a source at the company said, because it would have been forbidden by the Network Code, the complex bundle of rules governing the use of the U.K. pipeline system.
While Transco had not previously said how much gas they were going to sell under the tender, traders had been speculating it would be between 80 and 120 million therms.
